target: Distinct A-band styles in both modes, typical competitive Arena games ten-plus turns per player; proposed working band 10-14, not a hard minimum or a measured result. Campaign XVII-XX difficult but beatable.

starters.rationale: Reserves and straightforward defense/attacks provide a reliable opening. Shared Crimson Offering delays one Mana; Scent now caps each Aura at three hostile Exposed draws per owner-round. Grade carried forward; reward acquisition may change early campaign tempo.
Improved Drone and Pulse Pistol help; large-machine setup is still resource hungry.

Pack damage and blood resources are productive early. Blood Tithe and Adrenal Surge each move one Mana to next turn; total Mana and HP costs are unchanged. Grade carried forward; reward acquisition may change early campaign tempo.

Efficient suit/cycling pool gives broad early flexibility; pool parity unresolved. Cut the Deck refunds only once per own turn across copies, reducing self-funding cycling. Grade carried forward; reward acquisition may change early campaign tempo.

Recurring Dagger and efficient Skills provide consistent damage. Rush of Blood+ moves one Mana to next own turn; base is unchanged. Grade carried forward; reward acquisition may change early campaign tempo.

Two starting totems offer immediate value before row investment. Wellspring and Spirit Offering preserve total Mana but delay part until next own turn. Grade carried forward; reward acquisition may change early campaign tempo.
Stance sequencing is strong but mistakes can expose the hero.

Starting Spell Power supplies an early spend/rebuild rhythm. Shared Fault Lines generation and Measured Ruin amplification are lower, even when not the primary engine. Grade carried forward; reward acquisition may change early campaign tempo.
Small Thralls and slower Fate/Consume development need protection.
Gun and drink setup can compete, but HP/Hangover management is less forgiving.

corrections: This snapshot follows 0.197.0/rules 80; all older JSON/Markdown/CSV assessments remain unchanged. All approved long-fight changes are now implemented, including candidate Bonelord and Deathwish protection. P4 remains as previously released.

All 30 overall central estimates are A-band hypotheses. Shatterer and Deathwish explicitly retain B+ downside risk. Removing S labels is a projection from slower growth, not evidence of measured parity; A+ ceilings and setup-dependent weak openings remain.

Campaign deep grades for several resource/burst engines fall from A+ to A; Shatterer and Brewmaster endgame become A- due to lower offense/sustain. Deathwish and Bonelord endgame concerns remain. Lower Arena burst is not proof of Campaign beatability.
